value: f is undefined at x = 3/2; left limit -1, right limit +1
why: At x = 3/2 the denominator 2x-3 vanishes so f is not even defined there, and the one-sided limits are -1 and +1; hence discontinuous (and therefore not continuous/differentiable). Option D 'non-zero' is a property of the values away from 3/2, not of the function AT x = 3/2.

sin|x| is a composition of the continuous maps x -> |x| and u -> sin u, so it is continuous on R; B is false (|x| is continuous, not differentiable at 0), C is false (same counterexample, f' need not even exist), D is false (|x|+1 is not differentiable at 0).
With u = log_10 x and v = log_x 10 = 1/u, du/dv = 1/(dv/du) = 1/(-1/u^2) = -u^2 = -(log_10 x)^2; sympy confirms the ratio of derivatives is -(ln x)^2/(ln 10)^2.

Taylor to second order: constant terms 2-3+1=0, linear 2-6+4=0, quadratic coefficient (1)(1) - 3(4)/2 + (16)/2 = 1-6+8 = 3, giving 3f''(0) = 3k; verified numerically with f = e^{3x} (k=9) where the limit is 27.

From y^2=P: 2yy'=P' and 2y'^2+2yy''=P'', so y^3y'' = P·P''/2 - P'^2/4; differentiating gives P·P'''/2, hence 2 d/dx(y^3 y'') = P P'''. Checked symbolically on a general cubic (difference simplifies to 0).

Rolle needs f(-2)=f(2) plus continuity and differentiability: x^3 gives -8 vs 8, 2x^3+3 gives -13 vs 19 (both fail the endpoint condition), pi|x| has equal endpoints but is not differentiable at 0; only 4x^4 satisfies all three.
f'(x) = 4x - 1/x = (4x^2-1)/x, which is positive for -1/2<x<0 and for x>1/2; spot values f'(-0.25)=+3, f'(-0.75)=-5/3, f'(0.25)=-3, f'(0.75)=+5/3 confirm the sign pattern.
y = 1/((x+1)^2+4) has dy/dx = 0 only at x = -1, where y = 1/4; y = 0 is a horizontal asymptote, never attained, so it is not a tangent line.
With hypotenuse h and side a, h+a=k fixed, area = (1/2)a√(h^2-a^2) = (1/2)a√(k(k-2a)); maximising a^2k(k-2a) gives a = k/3, h = 2k/3, so cos(theta) = a/h = 1/2 and theta = pi/3.
1+cos 8x = 2cos^2 4x, so the integrand is (1/2)sec^2 4x whose antiderivative is tan(4x)/8; numeric check of the definite integral over [0.01, 0.1] matches to 30+ digits.

value: x^2/2 + c (the integrand simplifies to x)
why: With t = arctan√((1-x)/(1+x)), cos 2t = (1-tan^2 t)/(1+tan^2 t) = (1-(1-x)/(1+x))/(1+(1-x)/(1+x)) = x, so the integral is ∫x dx; numeric check over [0,0.5] gives 0.125 = (0.5)^2/2.
12 - x^2 - 4x = 16 - (x+2)^2, so the antiderivative is arcsin((x+2)/4); evaluating from -2 to 0 gives arcsin(1/2) - arcsin(0) = pi/6, matched numerically to 40 digits.
The limits sum to pi/2, so the substitution x -> pi/2 - x turns the integrand into √(tan x)/(1+√(tan x)); adding gives 2I = pi/3 - pi/6 = pi/6, so I = pi/12 (numeric quadrature agrees to 40 digits).
Split at x=1: ∫_0^1(1-x)dx = 1/2 and ∫_1^4(x-1)dx = 9/2, total 5; numeric quadrature returns exactly 5.0.
Applying x -> pi/2 - x turns the integrand into cos^100/(sin^100+cos^100); the two add to 1, so 2I = pi/2 and I = pi/4, confirmed by direct quadrature (0.78539816...).
The curves meet at x = ±4, so area = ∫_{-4}^{4}(16 - x^2)dx = 128 - 128/3 = 256/3 (sympy exact).

y^2 = x needs x >= 0, so only the branch y = x of y = |x| is relevant; they meet at (0,0) and (1,1) and area = ∫_0^1(√x - x)dx = 2/3 - 1/2 = 1/6 (sympy exact). The branch y = -x lives in x<0 where the parabola does not exist, so it encloses nothing.
Order is the highest derivative present, which is d^3y/dx^3; the exponents 2, 2, 5 affect the degree, not the order.

Multiplying through by y''' clears the fraction: (y'')^5 y''' + 4(y'')^3 + (y''')^2 = y''' sin x; the highest derivative is y''' so m = 3, and its highest power in this polynomial form is 2, so n = 2.
Parabolas with axis along y-axis are x^2 = 4a(y-k); differentiating gives 2x = 4a y' and 2 = 4a y'', so eliminating 4a yields 2x = (2/y'')y', i.e. x y'' - y' = 0.
